title: Maximal Fisher Budget Forces Blind Directions in Bipartite Collective SU(d) Metrology
authors: Tariq Aziz, Naeem Akhtar, Dong Wang, Augusto Smerzi
abstract: For pure two-qudit probes used in a single fixed setting to estimate a common SU(d) transformation, maximal total Fisher sensitivity and full local identifiability are mutually exclusive. We derive exact identities that determine the trace of the quantum Fisher information matrix from two measurable probe properties: exchange symmetry and collective polarization. Every maximizer is exchange symmetric and maximally entangled. Its Fisher matrix has equal sensitivity in every visible direction, while $d(d-1)/2$ generator directions are blind. More generally, weak compatibility, defined by vanishing mean generator commutators, forces at least $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ blind directions for every pure bipartite probe. A probe-defined antiunitary invariant classifies the complete Fisher spectrum at maximal entanglement, and approaches to the optimum that preserve exchange symmetry have a divergent Holevo cost. The bipartite obstruction is sharp in particle number: for $N\geq 3$, generalized GHZ probes can satisfy weak compatibility, attain the corresponding $N$-partite Fisher trace bound, and retain full local identifiability. Hence, Fisher sensitivity, weak compatibility, identifiability, and attainable precision are distinct resources in quantum metrology with noncommuting generators.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes the limits of quantum parameter estimation using bipartite probes under $SU(d)$ symmetry. It derives exact mathematical identities demonstrating that maximal Fisher sensitivity conflicts with full local identifiability, leading to inherent 'blind directions' in the measurement spectrum. The findings establish a hierarchy among distinct resources—sensitivity, compatibility, and identifiability—in non-commuting generator systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental trade-offs between achieving maximal total Fisher sensitivity, ensuring full local identifiability, and satisfying weak compatibility constraints in quantum metrology.
main_result: It establishes exact identities linking the Fisher information trace to measurable probe properties, showing that maximizing sensitivity forces blind directions unless generalized GHZ probes are used for $N \ge 3$.
method: The analysis involves deriving exact sum rules relating the Fisher matrix and incompatibility measures, utilizing structural decompositions of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(d)$, and comparing bounds derived from different probe symmetries.
model_or_system: The system is a pure bipartite quantum probe state used to estimate an unknown collective $SU(d)$ transformation. The analysis focuses on the structure of the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) associated with this estimation process.
